niche.habitat: Mid-tropospheric convective belts (5–10 km altitude), persistent cumulonimbus anvils
niche.diet: Atmospheric ions, lightning-fixed nitrates/sulfates, suspended aerosol organics, dissolved storm-water droplets
niche.active: Diurnal (peak during daytime thermals and afternoon squalls)

body: 1.8 m wingspan, biradial symmetry, four tapering charge-siphon arms, internal gas-foam lattice, sulfur-ceramic dermal plates, blue-green bioluminescent gut lining

chains.trait: Tapered, graphite-like siphon arms that crackle
links: Ion flux drives proton pumps in dermal tissue

skill.effect: Drain 15% HP from target to restore 12 stamina

chains.weakness: Prolonged contact with water shorts the siphon circuit, reducing ATP yield by 40%
observe: Sudden static hum in calm air

journal.en: It doesn't bite; it drinks the air.

journal.en: A living kite woven from storm and stone.

body_plan.origin: diverged from a benthic filter-feeding lineage that colonized convective updrafts during the late Aridification; convergent with aerial jellyfish but reinforced for charge capture

temperament: Patient, drift-predatory, highly territorial over updraft corridors, docile to non-threatening low-energy life
secrets: If you stand downwind of a roosting adult during a calm evening, the static charge will make your hair stand up and your tools hum.
Cracking its dermal plates releases trapped ionized gas that can be condensed into a potent fertilizer for Ochre Reach crops.
Its blue-green bioluminescence matches the atmospheric transmission window; ancient navigators used herds of them as living compasses during fog season.
moments: A squall breaks at dusk; it uncurls its siphon arms, and the storm answers. For three seconds, the air itself glows blue-green as it feeds, leaving only the smell of ozone and wet stone.

journal.en: First sight: a silhouette stitching through cumulonimbus anvils, trailing faint blue sparks.
Second sight: roosting in sulfur vents, plates blackened, siphons twitching at the barometric drop.
